title: The Dungeon of Black Company
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Kinji, a wealthy, idle NEET, is transported to a fantasy world and immediately forced into debt labor at an exploitative mining company. Arrogant and cunning, he schemes to beat the world's economy and get rich by any means, with the lizardman Wanibe and the hungry dragon-girl Rim beside him. A satire of Japan's 'black company' work culture.
life_message: Played as satire: exploitative work systems are absurd, and so is the selfish greed of the man trying to game them.

content.note: Monster incidents; workers at risk of dying from overwork (ANN).
Fan service, a 'bevy of babes' and Rim's nude 'little girl' form (ANN); MU Nudity, MangaDex Loli tag.
Overwork and abuse of workers (MU Overwork, Abused Protagonist).
Kinji is arrogant and exploitative, 'zero redeeming features' (ANN); MU Megalomania, Cunning Male Lead.
Money obsession in 'a land where money is everything' (Seven Seas blurb); satire of corporate exploitation (ANN; MU Corrupt Organization).

dominant: Marxism (labor exploitation satire), Consumerism (critiqued), Might makes right

frames.aligns: Exploitation of workers satirized, echoing the dignity of labor.
frames.concerns: Kinji's greed is the comic engine; nude child-form dragon girl (ANN).
Avarice and lust played for laughs.
Nudity including a childlike form; schemer as hero.

frames.aligns: Hard work's value contrasted with idleness.
Craving for wealth shown as absurd.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Arrogant lead fights for status (MU Arrogant Protagonist).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyal to a few coworkers only (ANN, McNulty).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Corporate hierarchy and debt slavery (MU Slavery, Company).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Debt, overwork and survival (Seven Seas blurb).

folkways.japan: 'Black company' (burakku kigyou) is Japanese slang for firms that exploit staff with unpaid overtime; the series satirizes this.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers discuss the satire and its unlikeable lead but do not call it heavy-handed or subtle.
delivery.note: The company and Kinji both stand for greed, and the satire targets both.

winners_losers: Kinji is the focus but reviewers find him unsympathetic; exploited workers and Wanibe carry the moral counterweight.
